change_note: risk/1.5 -> risk/1.6: registry_id; implementation_version cites risk/1.6; common.lookback.default_view: an active return refused by its portfolio leg TWR(g_0, g_n] is a history refusal (Ruling 7.7 (1.6)); common.corporate_action_treatment_benchmark and the two ETF-proxy rows of common.states_benchmark: a disputed ETF print withholds that day only, a disputed corporate action breaks the chain at its ex-date (Ruling 5.5 (1.6)). No entry-level text changes. RISK_1.0 to RISK_1.5_REGISTRY.json stay unchanged as records (Ruling 9.2 (1.2)).
status: Part of the text of risk/1.6 (methodology/CP4_RISK_CONVENTIONS.md Ruling 9.3). Any change to any entry is a convention change and gets a new id (Ruling 9.2). The engine's registry is loaded from this file or tested equal to it, and the id is read from 'registry_id', never from the file name; manifests record registry_id and the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON as registry_digest.

schema.notation: As risk/1.0 section 0: n periods (g_{k-1}, g_k]; r_k portfolio TWR, b_k benchmark return, rf_k risk-free return; d_k = r_k - rf_k; x_k = b_k - rf_k; a_k = r_k - b_k; mean(z) = (1/n) sum z_k; s2(z) = sum (z_k - mean(z))^2 / (n - 1); S_zw = sum (z_k - mean(z)) (w_k - mean(w)); A = periods per year.

allowed.DAILY: a period ends at every Monday to Friday (calendar weekdays)
allowed.MONTHLY: a period ends on the last calendar day of each month

frequency.valuation_at_grid_date: each listing at the official close of its own latest session on or before the grid date; each currency at the ECB fixing of the grid date (performance/1.12 Ruling 1.7)

lookback.rule: B from the request (performance Ruling 5.4 end-of-month rule); observations are the full grid periods inside [B, E]; stubs excluded and declared; never silently shortened (Rulings 2.3, 7.2)
lookback.default_view: A service-layer composition, not a metric (Ruling 7.7 (1.2), PD-0040): the default request is sent; if its result is INSUFFICIENT_DATA with a detail in {WINDOW_BEFORE_INCEPTION, WINDOW_BEFORE_SNAPSHOT, PERIOD_INSUFFICIENT, ZERO_CAPITAL_PERIOD}, or (1.6) it is an active return whose portfolio leg TWR(g_0, g_n] is INSUFFICIENT_DATA (any cause of the portfolio's own history), MAX_AVAILABLE is sent and shown with its own window, observation count and state, and the refused result stays in the evidence. A benchmark-side or risk-free cause is never a trigger. Neither result is relabelled.

common.current_mode: In Current mode at instant t: E = D_c(t) (performance Ruling 1.7 (1.12)), and every input is read from M_t, the files of M retrieved at or before t. A benchmark level, an ECB fixing (by its publication time) or a risk-free quote is used only if its scheduled close or publication is at or before t and it is in M_t. One not yet due at t is neither used nor counted as missed; one due at t but not in M_t is missed (Ruling 5.8 (1.3)).
common.reason_rule: One reason_code per result, by performance Ruling 1.5 (1.1), chosen only among the causes whose own state level equals the result's state. The observation-count rule is a cause with no code (LIMITED for insufficient_below <= n < available_from; INSUFFICIENT_DATA below), as are the degenerate cases and ZERO_CAPITAL_PERIOD. A coded cause at a lower level never supplies the reason; it stays in the details and lineage (Ruling 7.3 (1.3)). A refused window (WINDOW_BEFORE_INCEPTION, WINDOW_BEFORE_SNAPSHOT) is combined with the window-independent causes only (no selection, series not in M, price return, no risk-free source), never with window-dependent ones (Ruling 7.3 (1.5)).
common.selection_rule: The primary benchmark in force at a pinned selection-log version v (Ruling 5.6 (1.4)): records with seq <= v; a REVERSAL voids the SELECT or CLEAR it names; a replacement (corrects_selection_id) takes the order position of the record it corrects; the record in force is the live SELECT or CLEAR with the latest position (IN_FORCE or CLEARED); none live: NONE; a version that holds a REVERSAL of a correction pair but not its replacement is refused. A REVERSAL of a REVERSAL is refused at append. The engine never substitutes a benchmark.
common.manifest_intermediates: Every CP4 result's manifest records the exact rationals of Ruling 9.4 (1.4) for its metric (n, the means, the sums of squares and products, the risk-free mean, Q), never presented, included in the result digest.

minimum_observations_statistical.rule: insufficient_below = observations any full 1-year window yields; available_from = observations any full 3-year window yields (Ruling 7.1). Between them: LIMITED with the value.

minimum_observations_window_fact.rule: a window fact, like the TWR: no statistical minimum; one full period (Ruling 7.1)

common.fx_treatment: Computed in the reporting currency R. Every grid date is valued at the ECB fixing u(g); every flow at its own date's fixing (performance Rulings 1.2, 4.3). No native-currency statistic for a multi-currency scope (Ruling 0.1).
common.fx_treatment_benchmark: The benchmark level is translated into R at the same ECB fixing u(g) as the portfolio, unhedged (Ruling 5.3).
common.corporate_action_treatment: Through the ledger valuations: raw closes times ledger quantities; splits are value-continuous; dividends and other income are in the TWR; a split suppression reaches the periods whose valuations it suppresses (SOURCE_CONFLICT) (Ruling 2.1).
common.corporate_action_treatment_benchmark: The benchmark must be a total-return series (net or gross, as published) or an engine-built ETF proxy from the ETF's RAW closes and its CORROBORATED or SINGLE_SOURCE cash dividends and splits. Until a resolution record: a disputed ETF print is withheld for that day only and the chain links around it; a disputed dividend or split breaks the chain at its ex-date, so only ratios spanning it are unavailable (Rulings 5.4, 5.5 (1.6)).

states_window_and_series.condition: requested base before an account's snapshot
no full grid period in the window
a period with no capital at any time
a period return is AVAILABLE + STALE_DATA

states_risk_free.condition: no admitted risk-free series for R
no quote on or before a period's start
a period's quote 5 or more publications stale
a period's quote 2 to 4 publications stale
the publication calendar does not cover

states_benchmark.condition: no primary benchmark selected (or selection cleared)
the selected benchmark has no series in M
no level on or before a grid date
a level 5 or more calculation days stale
a level 2 to 4 calculation days stale
two sources of the benchmark disagree, beyond the precision bound, on the level used at a grid date (until a resolution record)
ETF proxy: a cash dividend or split of the ETF in DISAGREEMENT, for a ratio of levels that spans its ex-date (until a resolution record)
ETF proxy: the ETF's price sources DISAGREE on the print a grid date uses (until a resolution record)
the benchmark's translation into R fails

common.comparability_two_leg: Disclose LIMITED temporal comparability when the legs' scheduled instants differ (SEAM) or when at any grid date the legs' session lags differ (LAGGED). A disclosure, never a state (Ruling 8.2).
common.limitation_actual_history: Describes the portfolio as actually held over the window (Ruling 0.2), not today's holdings at today's weights.
common.limitation_daily: At DAILY frequency the legs of a cross-market portfolio are measured at closes 12 to 14 hours apart and closed-market days give zero returns; cross-market covariances and dispersions are biased toward zero (Epps effect). WEEKLY is the default for this reason (PRD 14).

entries.human_definition: How widely the portfolio's periodic returns in the reporting currency varied around their average over the window, scaled to a year.
entries.annualization_convention: square-root-of-time: x sqrt(A); A = 260 DAILY, 52 WEEKLY, 12 MONTHLY
data_inputs: the portfolio's periodic TWR series in R (Rulings 2.1-2.5)
entries.missing_data_handling: common.states_window_and_series, then common.states_count; never dropped, filled or re-gridded (Ruling 2.5)
known_limitations: The sqrt(A) scaling assumes serially uncorrelated periodic returns.
common.limitation_daily
common.limitation_actual_history
A value of 0 means the portfolio's value in R did not vary over the window (for example cash in R); it is a fact about the window.

wording.must_keep: window, frequency and observation count; when LIMITED, the count and the thresholds in the same unit

entries.metric_name: Downside deviation below the risk-free rate (annualized)
entries.human_definition: The root-mean-square of the periods' shortfalls below the risk-free rate over the window, scaled to a year. Periods above the rate count as zero shortfall.
entries.formula: sqrt(A * (1/n) * sum_k min(0, d_k)^2), d_k = r_k - rf_k
data_inputs: the portfolio's periodic TWR series in R
the risk-free series of R (Ruling 4.3)
entries.risk_free_rate_dependency: the 13-week sovereign series of the reporting currency, quote at each period's start, simple accrual over the period's calendar days (Rulings 4.1-4.4); target = rf_k
known_limitations: It measures shortfall below the risk-free rate, not losses: uninvested cash earning nothing has a positive value, about the annual rate divided by sqrt(A).
Divides by all n periods (target semideviation), not by the number of shortfall periods.
Unavailable for a reporting currency with no admitted risk-free series.
common.limitation_actual_history

wording.must_keep: that the threshold is the risk-free rate; the caveat that it is not a measure of losses

entries.human_definition: The largest fall, within the window, from a high point of the portfolio's cumulative return (the window's starting value included) to a later low point.
entries.formula: W_0 = 1 at the base g_0; W_k = W_{k-1}(1 + r_k); M_k = max_{0<=j<=k} W_j; MDD = min_k (W_k / M_k - 1)
data_inputs: the portfolio's periodic TWR series in R
known_limitations: peak_rule WITHIN_WINDOW_FROM_BASE: history before the window does not enter; it is not a drawdown from the all-time high (Ruling 1.1).
Sampled at the grid dates: a coarser frequency never shows a deeper drawdown (Ruling 1.4 RD-4).
A short window shows only what happened in it.
common.limitation_actual_history

wording.must_keep: the window and the peak and trough dates

entries.human_definition: The window's average periodic return above the risk-free rate, annualized, divided by the window's annualized volatility.
entries.formula: (A * mean(d)) / (sqrt(A) * s(r)) = sign(mean(d)) * sqrt(A * mean(d)^2 / s2(r))
entries.annualization_convention: numerator arithmetic (x A); denominator square-root-of-time (x sqrt(A)); not based on the annualized TWR
data_inputs: the portfolio's periodic TWR series in R
the risk-free series of R
entries.missing_data_handling: common.states_window_and_series, common.states_risk_free, common.states_count; s2(r) = 0 -> INSUFFICIENT_DATA, detail ZERO_VOLATILITY
known_limitations: Its numerator is an arithmetic mean excess return, not the annualized TWR minus the rate.
Its denominator is the volatility of returns (equal to the volatility shown), not of excess returns (Sharpe 1994's form; equal when the rate is constant).
Statistically fragile: over one year of weekly data its standard error is about 1.
common.limitation_actual_history

wording.must_keep: the risk-free series and the window; LIMITED caveat

entries.human_definition: The window's average periodic return above the risk-free rate, annualized, divided by the downside deviation below that rate.
entries.formula: (A * mean(d)) / DD = sign(mean(d)) * sqrt(A * mean(d)^2 * n / sum_k min(0, d_k)^2)
data_inputs: the portfolio's periodic TWR series in R
the risk-free series of R
entries.risk_free_rate_dependency: as risk_downside_deviation (the same target in numerator and denominator)
entries.missing_data_handling: common.states_window_and_series, common.states_risk_free, common.states_count; s2(r) = 0 -> ZERO_VOLATILITY; no d_k < 0 -> NO_DOWNSIDE_OBSERVATIONS
known_limitations: Undefined for a riskless path (volatility 0), where it would otherwise equal -sqrt(A) whatever the rate.
Undefined when no period fell below the rate.
common.limitation_actual_history

wording.must_keep: that the threshold is the risk-free rate

entries.metric_name: Beta to the primary benchmark (historical, model-based)
entries.human_definition: The slope of the portfolio's periodic returns on the benchmark's over the window: how much the portfolio's return moved, on average, per unit of the benchmark's, in the reporting currency.
entries.formula: S_rb / S_bb (OLS slope of the market model r_k = alpha_m + beta b_k + e_k, total returns in R)
data_inputs: the portfolio's periodic TWR series in R
the primary benchmark's total-return series translated into R (Rulings 5.1-5.6)
entries.benchmark_dependency: the user's primary benchmark (selection record named on the result), total return, translated into R unhedged at u(g)
known_limitations: An OLS estimate with sampling error; its variance v_beta is in lineage, not presented.
common.limitation_daily
On total returns, not excess returns: with a time-varying rate the excess-return slope differs slightly; equal when the rate is constant.
common.limitation_actual_history

wording.must_keep: benchmark, window, frequency, observation count, the comparability disclosure; no 'more/less than the market' unless a documented rule supports it (PD-0014 2.3)

entries.metric_name: R-squared against the primary benchmark (historical, model-based)
entries.human_definition: The share of the variation of the portfolio's periodic returns over the window that the market-model regression on the benchmark accounts for.
data_inputs: as risk_beta
known_limitations: Describes the fit over the window, not a causal relationship.
common.limitation_daily
common.limitation_actual_history

entries.human_definition: Over the window, the portfolio's average return above the risk-free rate minus beta times the benchmark's average return above that rate, annualized. A historical model output, not a measure of skill.
entries.formula: A * (mean(d) - beta * mean(x)), d_k = r_k - rf_k, x_k = b_k - rf_k, beta from risk_beta
entries.annualization_convention: arithmetic (x A); not the vertical distance between geometric window returns and an ex-post market line
data_inputs: the portfolio's periodic TWR series in R
the primary benchmark's total-return series in R
the risk-free series of R
entries.missing_data_handling: common.states_window_and_series, common.states_benchmark, common.states_risk_free, common.states_count; S_bb = 0 -> ZERO_BENCHMARK_VARIANCE
known_limitations: Historical and model-based (PRD 17.2); not a measure of manager skill.
Uses the total-return beta; equals the excess-return regression intercept when the rate is constant.
Statistically noisy over short windows.
common.limitation_daily
common.limitation_actual_history

shown_with: risk-free series and its window mean

wording.must_keep: 'historical, model-based; not a measure of skill' in the same unit as the value, at every depth

entries.metric_name: Active return against the primary benchmark
entries.human_definition: The portfolio's time-weighted return over the window minus the benchmark's return over the same window, both in the reporting currency.
data_inputs: the portfolio's TWR over the effective window
benchmark_return
entries.missing_data_handling: the state of TWR(g_0, g_n] (performance Ruling 5.5), and common.states_benchmark at g_0 and g_n only (Ruling 6.9 (1.1)); a grid period of (g_0, g_n] with no capital at any time -> INSUFFICIENT_DATA, detail ZERO_CAPITAL_PERIOD (Ruling 6.9 (1.5))
known_limitations: Arithmetic difference of two compounded window returns (so it equals the difference of the two displayed returns); the geometric form is not used.
Not the numerator of the information ratio.
Undefined over a window in which the portfolio held no capital for a whole grid period; a period with capital for part of its days counts, a stated limitation (Ruling 2.4).
